next_action.description: DO NOT WRITE CODE FIRST. Open the session with /mpi-brainstorm on the masking system. The user has ideas that may change how masking works as a whole, and they explicitly want options explored before any further mask implementation, because building MPI-379 first would cause large drift. Bring these into the brainstorm as inputs, not as settled constraints: (1) the detect flow is currently TWO ComfyUI round trips - run 1 returns only SEGSPreview thumbnail CROPS which carry no position, and run 2 returns masks for the picked indices only, which is why nothing is hoverable before you pick; (2) the user has already chosen option A for that - the first run should return ALL region masks, which both enables hover AND makes picking client-side so the second round trip disappears, leaving the flow FASTER than it ships today; (3) SAM3 text masking is cancelled and SAM3 cannot enumerate a scene; (4) YOLO is the only thing we have that enumerates objects without being told what to look for, and a COCO -seg model would widen it to 80 everyday classes; (5) the mask family is Detect + Points shipped, Shapes (MPI-368) queued, Text dropped. After the brainstorm, re-validate MPI-379's recorded decisions and only then implement. If the brainstorm defers mask work, MPI-378 (Tab flipper) is fully specced and independent.

key_decisions: MPI-372 (SHIPPED): mask tools keep the PromptBox AND the canvas. swapToPreview() is a VRAM optimisation - it destroys MpiCanvas to free GPU texture backing, and MpiMaskedImagePreview is a strict subset of the canvas - so a mask tool never swaps. NEVER add a surface swap to a mask tool.

MPI-372 (SHIPPED): mask state is published as it CHANGES, from the canvas stroke-end signal (_endMaskStroke -> onMaskStrokeEnd -> _publishMaskState -> evaluateMask -> mask-ready), emitting only on a flip. ANY new mask tool that creates a mask by another route - a shape commit, a detection - MUST emit mask-ready itself or the op strip never unlocks. This matters directly for MPI-368 Shapes.

MPI-372 (SHIPPED): the rail is the source of truth for the armed canvas tool; both viewer-reload paths share _syncViewerToolMode(). Never clear the mode before loadEntry - it captures and restores it itself.
MPI-372 (SHIPPED): workspace:set-operation no longer forces prompt mode. Its ONLY emitter is the PromptBox op strip, which lives inside the box. Do not reintroduce the force.

MPI-361 PHASE B CANCELLED, with proof. Probed the SHIPPED engine (engine/ComfyUI_windows_portable, ComfyUI 0.28.0 on :8188 - NOT the G:\ComfyUi bench): SAM3_Detect is core (comfy_extras.nodes_sam3) so the node was free, but reading its execute() shows it is STRICTLY prompt-driven - points, box and text are the only paths, and with none supplied it returns a zero mask. There is NO automatic-mask-generation node among the engine's 1842 registered node types. So SAM3 can never enumerate a scene, and the text selection it does offer the user judged unintuitive ('selection should be discovered, not described'). Do not resurrect this without re-reading MPI-361 validation.md.

SALVAGED FROM THE SAM3 PROBE, worth keeping: SAM3_Detect.positive_coords / negative_coords take JSON PIXEL coords directly ([{"x":int,"y":int}]), which is far cleaner than Phase A's shipped r=8 / r=4 radius-straddling hack for point polarity and would collapse the two-threshold split. And individual_masks:true emits per-object masks. Relevant input for the brainstorm if points are ever reworked.

MPI-379 DECISION (option A, chosen by the user but NOT implemented): the first Detect run must return ALL region masks rather than only the picked ones. Today run 1 returns only SEGSPreview thumbnail CROPS - no position - and run 2 returns masks for picks only, which is exactly why nothing is hoverable before picking. Returning everything on run 1 enables hover AND makes picking client-side, deleting the second round trip. Touches comfy_workflows/img_auto_mask.json, runAutoMask and commandExecutor.

MPI-379 DECISION: clicking a hovered region selects it only while a THIRD 'Select' mode is active in MpiMaskStrip (Brush | Erase | Select). The strip's brush radio has NO neutral state and defaults to 'brush', so left-click always paints - hence the conflict. Hover highlights in every mode; painting over a detected region must keep working, which is why click-to-select cannot simply take priority.
MPI-379 DECISION: prefer the -seg COCO YOLO variant (yolov8n-seg.pt, ~7MB) over plain yolov8n.pt, because segmentation masks make the hover highlight a real outline rather than a rectangle.

MPI-378 DECISION: once Tab is the workspace flipper, DROP the workspace radial entirely. RADIAL_ITEMS and the PAGE_GALLERY / PAGE_GROUP_HISTORY setContextItems calls go; the radial survives only as the dev-gated Ctrl+Tab ring, and Models stays reachable via the PromptBox model button + the ui:open-model-picker event, which must keep working. Note the radial was never broken - since MPI-356 it holds ONE item and MpiRadialMenu._onTabDown short-circuits any single-item context, firing it without drawing a ring.

Detectors are declared in js/data/modelConstants/assetDeps.js as engineAsset:true entries (boot-installed, self-healing, never GC'd), R2-hosted at models.cubric.studio. The UI list is DETECTION_MODELS in MpiCanvasViewer.js, exposed via el.getDetectionModels() so options compounds do not fork it.

OPEN, NOT DECIDED: the existing 4 detector radios are one-class-per-entry; a COCO model detects 80 classes at once. How that presents in the control must be settled with the user before wiring part 2 of MPI-379.

context.verification_recipe: The live-app harness that proved MPI-372 is reusable and cheap. A Node script requiring playwright by ABSOLUTE path (c:/AI/Mpi/Cubric-Vision/node_modules/playwright) so it runs from the scratchpad; goto with waitUntil 'domcontentloaded' NOT 'networkidle' (the app holds SSE streams open, so networkidle never settles); a fresh page has no project, so import /js/services/projectService.js and call listProjects() + openProject() before router.navigate(PAGE_GROUP_HISTORY, { groupId }). Rail buttons carry the tool NAME in [data-info] ('Detect', 'Points', 'Crop', 'Prompt'), NOT the mode key. ALWAYS pair a green run with a NEGATIVE CONTROL: back the files up, `git show HEAD:<path>` over them, re-run, restore, and diff to prove the restore. A green run with no negative control proves nothing about what the harness actually measures.
